sentences.text: Order:

This Criminal Petition is filed by the petitioner-accused No.1 seeking to quash the proceedings against him in C.C.No.841 of 2024 on the file of learned VI Additional Metropolitan Magistrate,
Medchal-Malkajgiri District, Uppal at L.B. Nagar, registered for the offences under Section 498A I.P.C. and Section 3 of the Dowry Prohibition Act.
2.

entities.text:
VI Additional Metropolitan Magistrate,
Medchal-Malkajgiri District, Uppal
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Heard Sri V.N.R. Chaitanya, learned counsel for the petitioner and Sri Jithender Rao Veeramalla,
learned Additional Public Prosecutor for respondent No.1-State.
3. Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the petitioner is the husband of respondent No.2-de facto complainant.
There are no specific allegations against the petitioner.
The petitioner has never harassed the de facto complainant and he never suspected the fidelity of the de facto complainant, as alleged by the de facto complainant.
He further submitted that the present complaint is lodged with all vague allegations.
He, therefore, prayed to quash the proceedings in the present C.C. against the petitioner.
2 ETD,J 4.
Learned Additional Public Prosecutor submitted that there are specific allegations of harassment meted out on the de facto complainant in the hands of the petitioner.

He further submitted that after begetting two children, the petitioner started harassing the de facto complainant both physically and mentally by saying that the children were not born through him, duly suspecting the fidelity of the de facto complainant.
He, therefore, prayed to dismiss the Criminal Petition.

5. Perused the record.
6.
The petitioner herein is none other than the husband of the de facto complainant.

The contents of the complaint and the statement of LW.1 (de facto complainant) point out specific allegations of harassment to attract the offence under Section 498A I.P.C. against the petitioner herein.
It is alleged that the petitioner herein used to suspect the fidelity of the de facto complainant.
The allegations are serious in nature.
The truth or otherwise of the allegations would be made out during the course of trial.
Hence, it is deemed appropriate to dispense with the attendance of the petitioner before the trial Court.
